## Key dialect decisions (from `specs/ini.md`)

- **Continuation before escapes**: odd trailing-backslash runs are markers, even runs are literals (`k=a\\\` → `a\b=1`), verified against the full N-table.
- **Quoted values never span lines**: a value whose first non-blank char is a quote is parsed on its first physical line only; an open quote is an error "whether or not a later line would close it". Only unquoted values continue.
- **Continuation lines contribute text, not syntax**: their `=`, `:`, quotes and comment markers are ordinary (comment search is bounded to the first physical line's contribution).
- **Strict section headers** (`[name]` exactly, nested brackets/empty/trailing text rejected), quote-wrapping stripped, re-opening and last-wins handled by map insertion; empty sections are materialised eagerly.
- **Comments**: full-line `;`/`#`, inline only when preceded by whitespace; escapes decoded per carrier (`\n\r\t` unquoted/double, `\\` everywhere, `\"`/`\'` respectively, everything else kept verbatim).

## What it does

- Every value is reassembled across partial reads: `read_exact` loops until complete, so all decoders work over a one-byte-per-call reader; end of stream mid-value raises.
- Varints: minimal output, any ≤10-byte input accepted (non-minimal included), bits past the 64th dropped, 11th byte raises; 32-bit readers take the low 32 bits.
- Keys: `(field << 3) | wire_type`, rejecting wire types 6/7 and field number 0, returning groups (3/4).
- `int32`/`enum` sign-extend to ten bytes; `sint32`/`sint64` zigzag; fixed-width little-endian with bit-exact floats; length prefixes bounded to `0..=2^31-1`; packed fields decoded through a `LimitedReader`; `read_unknown` skips varint/8/len/4 and whole nested groups, raising on mismatched end tags, stray EGROUP and undefined types.
- UTF-8 is validated via the core strict decoder (overlong, surrogates, >U+10FFFF, truncation and stray continuations rejected; NUL/C1/BOM kept). `write_string` pre-checks unpaired surrogates so it raises rather than aborting.
- Malformed input always raises; nothing on the read path aborts. Length-delimited payloads are gathered in bounded chunks so a bogus huge prefix raises instead of forcing a giant allocation.

## Caveat (the one thing I could not verify)

9 corpus files (`invalid/encoding/bad-utf8-*`, `bad-codepoint`, `utf16-*`) contain byte sequences that are **not valid UTF-8**. The required API takes a `StringView`, which is already valid Unicode, so those inputs are unconstructible through it; the harness reports them as `SKIP`, not as passes. A byte-oriented `parse` would reject them. I deliberately did **not** add a U+FFFD rejection hack to convert them into passes — that would be corpus-shaped behaviour rather than a correct TOML rule. This limitation is documented in the README.

Also documented: unbounded array/inline-table recursion depth (the spec sets no limit).
